item.title: Continuing Campus-Wide Walking Challenge & Monday Walking Group at Blackburn Center (Armour J. Blackburn University Center)
item.description:
Mon, 28 Sep 2026

Walking lowers the risk of heart disease, helps manage weight, and strengthens muscles. It also reduces stress, clears the mind, and improves daily mood. All staff and faculty are invited to join in a campus-wide walking challenge that started August 24 and goes until October 2. Participants can still enroll, set goals, and track daily steps. Each week, two $50 gift cards will be given out to participants who meet the daily step requirements; at the end of the challenge three $100 gift cards will be awarded. Registration required.

To support the challenge, an in-person walking group will meet every Monday (except Labor Day) in front of Blackburn Center. Led by Howard University Wellness Champion, Alisha McDougal, and supported by the HR Wellness and Benefits team, participants will gather and walk together in a shady area around campus. This in-person group walk will be repeated every Monday during the challenge. Please bring your walking shoes and water.

For more information, contact Alisha McDougal at Alisha.McDougal@Howard.edu or Onsite Health Coach, Katherine Smith, at Katherine.Smith@Evernorth.com.

item.title: BADGE Lecture Series - Black Wealth Across the American Century at Howard University School of Business Auditorium
item.description:
Wed, 30 Sep 2026

Black Wealth Across the American Century brings together scholarship, history, economics, and performance for a timely conversation examining Black economic life across the 20th century. Presented as part of the Black Arts, Design & Global Engagement (BADGE) Lecture Series, the program will explore connections between contemporary Black wealth research and August Wilson’s American Century Cycle, his landmark series of plays chronicling the Black experience across ten decades of American life.

The conversation will feature Dr. LaTanya White, National Associate and Mid-Atlantic Regional Director of the Howard University & PNC National Center for Entrepreneurship at the Howard University School of Business, and Dr. Khalid Y. Long, Associate Dean of Academic Affairs at the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts and President of the August Wilson Society. Through their respective perspectives in economic research, entrepreneurship, theatre, and cultural studies, Drs. White and Long will consider how Black communities have navigated wealth creation, economic opportunity, systemic barriers, and generational change—and how those realities are reflected in Wilson’s dramatic portrait of Black America. Dr. Raquel Monroe, Dean of the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, will provide opening remarks.

The event takes place Wednesday, September 30, 2026, from 4:00–6:00 p.m. in the Howard University School of Business Auditorium.

item.title: Understanding Student Financials: What Every Howard University Staff Member Should Know
item.description:
Wed, 30 Sep 2026

This series is intended to give university staff enough practical knowledge to confidently answer common questions, recognize when an issue needs specialized review, and route students to the correct office—without requiring staff to become financial aid or student accounts experts

The first session in this series will address Balances, FARs, and Registration Implications.

What does a student's account balance actually mean?What is the difference between a current balance, past-due balance, and anticipated financial aid?Why might BisonHub show a balance even when a student says their financial aid "covers everything"?What is a FAR?Does a pending FAR mean the student's balance has been resolved?What happens when a student has a past-due balance?What is the registration threshold?When is a student prevented from registering?When and how are financial holds removed?Can a hold be temporarily lifted so a student can register?What should staff tell a student who says, "Another office told me I could register"?Who can actually make decisions about a student's financial eligibility to register?Where should students be referred when the issue is financial aid versus an outstanding student account?

A funding request, anticipated resource, or pending adjustment is not the same as a resolved student account. Staff should understand the student's current financial position before advising them about registration next steps.
